chapter: A musical family and the old New Orleans bands
title: Chicago in 1932 with Bud Harris's stranded band
summary: Danny went to Chicago with vaudeville star Bud Harris's band, stayed at the Ritz, and was blocked from playing the Regal because of house-band rules.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: I know. He was nice... And so he knew me. After I met him, he knew me. And then, when I went to Chicago... Let me see, this was '32. I went there with Bud Harris. We stayed at a hotel of that a man owned that owned the Grand Terrace.
Yeah, we were staying at a hotel on the corner.

Yes, we stayed at the Ritz. I've got an aunt there and two or three cousins there. I'm not stranded. I just didn't visit right quick, you know? But I'm with the band. Because the band is stranded. We go there, and they wouldn't let them play the Palace. What was it, the Palace? They wouldn't let us play the Loews State... No, we played the Loews State. So then he was going to come up to the Regal. So they said "No, you've got to use the house band."
What's the name of the band? What band is it?
Bud Harris was a vaudeville star, a big-time star in vaudeville. He decided to get a band...
That was your first trip to Chicago, huh?
